A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BAM/GGD-BAM research. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable, and relocated content can be reliably matched.

before.justification: v2 reports original language-model evaluations, including perplexity, passkey retrieval, RULER results, ablations, and computational timing measurements.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds MMLU, ARC, LongBench v2, learned-parameter analyses, and context-extension loss measurements.

M1.justification: The GGD-BAM attention bias, parameterization, negative-beta extension, and optional SSMax remain unchanged. The lightweight context-extension fine-tuning described in v3 Appendix H.5 already appears in v2 Appendix F.5.

E1.justification: v3 adds MMLU, ARC-Easy, ARC-Challenge, and LongBench v2 evaluations, extending coverage to knowledge and reasoning questions, code understanding, dialogue history, in-context learning, and document QA. FineWeb training, Wikipedia/FineWeb perplexity, passkey retrieval, and RULER coverage are retained.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in corresponding retained experiments is unchanged. The new downstream and LongBench evaluations extend the existing large-model BAM SSMax versus RoPE SSMax comparison to additional benchmarks.

E3.justification: New LongBench evaluations specify 1B models and a 131k-token limit. The cost comparison drops the 8B configuration and adds VRAM measurement. Its caption changes from forward-pass timing in v2 Table 6 to backward-pass time/VRAM in v3 Table 8, although retained inference wording leaves the exact measurement procedure ambiguous.

E4.justification: v3 adds systematic analyses of learned beta/alpha clusters across training lengths and model scales (Section 3.3), SSMax parameter distributions, and loss versus position before and after context extension (Appendices H.4–H.5). These substantially expand evidence about attention specialization and extrapolation behavior. Existing ablations and their conditions are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions specify 100 timing samples and report timing means with standard deviations. v3 adds no training-seed information, repeated-training uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Changed timing means and deviations do not change the reporting practice.

E6.justification: v3 adds BAM SSMax/RoPE SSMax scores of 0.3716/0.3573 on MMLU, 0.5770/0.5715 on ARC-Easy, and 0.4132/0.4123 on ARC-Challenge (Table 3). LongBench overall scores are 28.6/24.2, with dialogue understanding tied at 35.0 (Table 6). Parameter and loss findings are also new. Original retrieval/perplexity results remain unchanged; timing entries are replaced, VRAM values added, and 8B timings removed, without establishing comparable speed changes.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, theorem substance, Appendix B proofs, and alternative interpretations of Z are retained. v3 omits the duplicate equation inside Theorem 1's box, but the same identity remains in its proof. Appendix I's derivations move to Appendix K.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: probabilistic positional priors, unification of NoPE and ALiBi, GGD-BAM, and improved long-context retrieval with minimal additional parameters. The headline 500-times-training-length claim is unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 3.3 newly interprets parameter clusters as local, retrieval, and more aggressive retrieval heads, and suggests stability and transferability from their recurrence across model scales. Appendix H.4 distinguishes learned SSMax scaling from query/key-dependent Z. Existing limitations and the main extrapolation interpretation remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 Table 8 newly discloses per-model VRAM footprints alongside revised runtime measurements. Appendix C's architecture, optimization settings, training budgets, GPU information, and BAM implementation details remain unchanged, as does the code-access link.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations for MMLU (Hendrycks et al.), ARC (Clark et al.), and LongBench v2 (Bai et al.). The related-work discussion and positioning relative to existing positional encodings remain substantively unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 moves the BAM matrix explanation into the main text, adds Section 3.3 and two evaluation appendices, and updates affiliations and acknowledgments. Most retained prose and the overall narrative order remain unchanged.

P2.justification: New parameter-cluster scatterplots, an SSMax histogram, loss curves, and downstream benchmark tables substantially expand the visual evidence. The scoring diagram moves from v2 Figure 5 in the appendix to v3 Figure 2 in the main text. The cost table is redesigned with paired Time/VRAM columns and removes the 8B column.

improvement.justification: The downstream evaluations and parameter/loss diagnostics broaden empirical support beyond v2's perplexity and synthetic retrieval evidence. The gain is limited by sparse new evaluation details and absent uncertainty estimates. New reporting problems also reduce its value: LongBench prose overstates a table containing a dialogue tie and a 4.4-point overall gap, while Table 8 mixes inference/backward-pass descriptions and is not reconciled with the retained timing-equivalence claim.
